audit_findings.title: Post-anchor debt-funded cash may be credited to equity without its matching cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $546.4 million, or $5.99 per share and 3.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The June 2026 note proceeds enter the cash bridge, while FY2025 OE predates the refinancing and the related July 2026 redemption.
audit_findings.evidence: Our most significant future cash requirements include interest and principal payments on the senior notes issuances described above, income tax payments, purchase obligations and registry fees related to the operation of certain top-level domains.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated date mismatch: the June 30 cash balance included $546.4 million of net refinancing proceeds, and the filing states that the old $550.0 million notes were redeemed on July 20. Removing those proceeds would reduce base value from $157.90 to about $151.91 per share. That correction is concrete but far below the $117.21 gap between the $292.08 market price and the $174.87 bull value, so it cannot change the current valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge using a post-July-20 balance sheet or subtract the $546.4 million net proceeds and incorporate the replacement notes' interest expense in the next OE period.

audit_findings.title: Advance customer cash may be double-counted as excess cash and future earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially non-excess advance collections enter the cash bridge while future OE capitalizes revenue recognized as the associated deferred-revenue obligations are performed.
audit_findings.evidence: As payment for domain name registrations and renewals are due in advance of the Company’s performance, the Company records these amounts as deferred revenues.
audit_findings.explanation: Advance billing is demonstrated, but double counting is not. At June 30, deferred revenue was $1,448.9 million and customer deposits were $78.6 million, compared with the $1,034.1 million cash-and-securities addition. The record does not identify required operating liquidity, trace the sources of cash, or show how working-capital changes enter OE, so the amount of genuinely excess cash and the valuation impact cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $1,034.1 million cash-and-securities balance to deferred revenue, customer deposits, refinancing proceeds and operating liquidity, then rerun with only demonstrably excess cash or an explicit deferred-revenue working-capital schedule.

audit_findings.title: The terminal value crosses the core contract-renewal cliffs
audit_findings.magnitude: $6,883.5 million of base operating PV, equal to 51.5% of operating PV and 47.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The terminal-growth assumption capitalizes OE beyond the 2029 .net and 2030 .com renewal dates without modeling possible changes in pricing, fees, obligations or operating rights.
audit_findings.evidence: Substantially all of our revenues are derived from our operation of the . com gTLD under our Cooperative Agreement with the DOC and our . com Registry Agreement as well as our operation of the . net gTLD under our .net Registry Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a material unresolved assumption rather than a demonstrated contract loss. Substantially all revenue depends on these agreements, and nearly half of base equity value is attributable to terminal value exposed to post-renewal economics. Presumptive renewal supports continuity but does not establish unchanged terms, so plausible renewal outcomes could materially change intrinsic value and the buy threshold.
audit_findings.action: Rerun bear, base and bull cases with explicit 2029 and 2030 renewal discontinuities, including lower pricing rights, higher registry or compliance costs, altered service obligations and a loss-or-transfer case.

audit_findings.title: Completed .web ownership may introduce costs absent from the historical anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-delegation launch, infrastructure, registry, legal and compliance costs could reduce OE, while the $806.3 million anchor predates delegation and includes no corresponding expense.
audit_findings.evidence: Any of these initiatives require significant resources, can subject us to regulatory scrutiny and/or negative publicity, and divert management attention from our existing business.
audit_findings.explanation: Delegation is completed, so this is no longer merely a prospective acquisition warning, but the supplied record demonstrates no omitted cost amount. The existing $145.2 million deposit does not quantify future operating obligations, and the confidential resolution was described as not material to the financial statements. The finding may affect value, but present evidence cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the assignment terms, post-delegation balance sheet, launch budget, registry-payment schedule and operating-cost forecast, then rerun OE and growth after including costs not represented in FY2025.

audit_findings.title: The stated share ceiling omits outstanding ESPP purchase options
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncounted ESPP purchase rights could increase the fully diluted share denominator and reduce value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Each participant is granted an option to purchase common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The exact August 2026 ESPP issuance is not supplied, so the omission remains unresolved. Its demonstrated scale is small: the filing reported only 0.2 million weighted-average potential shares from unvested RSUs and ESPP combined, equal to 0.22% of the 91.2 million valuation denominator. That denominator also exceeds the July 17 cover count of 90.3 million by 0.9 million shares, or about 1.0%, providing a substantially larger dilution allowance than the filed combined diluted increment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the August 2026 ESPP shares issued and outstanding purchase rights, reconcile them with repurchases after July 17, and update the denominator if total dilution exceeds the existing 0.9 million-share allowance.
